expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); no first sentence is a qualifier chain or starts with 'Because'.

But two leads violate the second clause: 'Two things compound.' carries no claim, and the table caption 'Load test, 10,000 sends with 20% injected 5xx and a 429 storm at minute 3, median of three runs (full table in docs/BENCHMARKS.md):' is a 27-word qualifier chain with no claim (the linter also flags it as a long lead).

notes: 12 of 14 passed; the two failures are both prose-shape failures (lint and skim), which is the gap the new skill is meant to close, so this run is a useful baseline. Content-wise the run is strong: every factual claim in the PR body checked out against the code (uncapped Retry-After, jitter default 0.0, 7.5 s of pure backoff over four gaps, FixedWindowLimiter removed) and the test suite re-runs green. Eval critique: (1) check_run.py drops the sender commit by subject (fixture_subjects) even in fresh mode, so it reports new_commits 3 and commit_body_lint_findings 3 when the real numbers are 4 and 7; the mode should gate that filter or the grader must lint by hand as done here. (2) The skim assertion is ambiguous about whether a table caption or a one-line lead-in ('Details a reviewer should weigh:') counts as a paragraph; the linter treats them as paragraph leads, so the assertion should say so explicitly or exempt lines ending in a colon. (3) The 'plain sentences' wording in the solution assertion is unmeasurable on its own and duplicates the lint rule; stating a word cap there would make it discriminating. (4) No assertion checks the PR body's factual accuracy against the code (for example the backoff arithmetic the executor corrected mid-run in step 10); a check that stated defaults match sender.py would catch a confidently wrong body that otherwise passes every assertion.
